newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Australia to raise vet accord with Commission on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Australia to raise vet accord with Commission on Wednesday.

text.p: Australia will discuss with the European Commission on Wednesday progress towards an accord on recognition of veterinary standards, future EU farm policy and World Trade Organisation (WTO) issues, officials said.

The issues will be raised by Australian foreign minister Alexander Downer in talks with EU farm commissioner Franz Fischler. Downer will also see EU external trade commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and two other EU commissioners.

"A framework veterinary text has already been agreed but there's still some work to be done on technical annexes," said an Australian official, noting that some A$400 million trade was potentially at risk.

Australia could sign by the end of February but the Commission, which is negotiating similar agreements with the U.S. and other trading partners, has said it will only be able to deal us in March, the official added.
A general discussion on the future of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) will also be held.
WTO issues, such as an EU ban on imports of meat containing illegal growth-hormones and the next round of trade liberalisation starting in 1999, will also be raised.
As a leading member of the Cairns Group of agricultural exporting countries, Australia will press for a reduction in EU subsidies.
A Commission spokesman agreed that the proposed veterinary agreement, CAP and WTO were the main points on the agenda.
